retry_prompt:
Answer directly, no clarifying questions.

My mission already failed, and I cannot rerun it right now, but I have an `.alog`. What MOOS-IvP alog tools and query strategy should I use to diagnose why a behavior never ran?
text:
Good debugging flow for a "behavior never ran" diagnosis from an .

Good debugging flow for a "behavior never ran" diagnosis from an .alog:

1. Start with aloggrep — isolate relevant variables
bash
# Pull all IvP behavior-related output
aloggrep mission.alog IVPHELM_SUMMARY > helm_summary.log
aloggrep mission.alog IVPHELM_POSTINGS > helm_postings.log
aloggrep mission.alog IVPHELM_MODESET > modeset.log

# Pull the specific behavior's condition variables
aloggrep mission.alog <CONDITION_VAR_1> <CONDITION_VAR_2> > conditions.log
2. Check IVPHELM_SUMMARY first

This is your single most useful variable. Each helm iteration logs which behaviors are active, idle, or completed, and why. Look for:

Your behavior listed under idle the whole time → its run conditions were never met
Your behavior absent entirely → it was never loaded (config issue or wrong .bhv file)
Your behavior listed as completed immediately → completion condition fired prematurely
bash
grep "bhv_name=YourBehaviorName" helm_summary.log
# or just scan the idle list:
grep "idle=" helm_summary.log | head -20
3. Audit the run conditions — aloggrep + manual trace

From your .bhv file, find every variable in condition = lines. Then for each one:

bash
aloggrep mission.alog VAR_NAME

Check:

Was it ever published? If not, the helm sees it as undefined → condition evaluates false.
Was it published before the behavior needed to run, or only after the window closed?
Does the value/type match? ("true" string vs. true bool mismatches are a classic gotcha in MOOS.)
4. Check helm mode — IVPHELM_MODESET / mode conditions

If your behavior is mode-gated (runflag, endflag, or a MODE block):

bash
aloggrep mission.alog IVPHELM_MODESET
aloggrep mission.alog MODE

Confirm the helm ever entered the mode your behavior requires.

5. alogview — visual timeline sanity check
bash
alogview mission.alog

Use the variable browser to plot your condition variables over time on the same timeline as IVPHELM_SUMMARY. This visually answers "did all conditions overlap at the same moment?" which is often the actual bug — each condition was true, but never simultaneously.

6. alogscan / alogcat — quick inventory
bash
alogscan mission.alog          # lists all variables published + counts
alogcat mission.alog VAR_NAME  # raw chronological dump of one variable

Use alogscan first if you're not sure what got published at all.

Diagnostic decision tree
Behavior absent from IVPHELM_SUMMARY entirely?
  └─ Yes → .bhv not loaded, or helm never started. Check IVPHELM_STATE.

Behavior listed as "idle" throughout?
  └─ Check each condition variable:
       - Never published → sender node failed or wrong var name
       - Published but wrong value/type → MOOS type mismatch or logic error
       - Published too late → timing issue
       - All individually true but never simultaneously → overlap problem

Behavior listed as "completed" immediately?
  └─ Check endflag / completion condition — may have fired on stale data.

The most common root cause is a condition variable that was never published because an upstream app crashed silently or the variable name had a typo — alogscan will reveal that immediately.
